articles.title: The Most Expensive Lego Sets You Can Buy in 2026
articles.summary: Playing with LEGOs is an expensive hobby.
articles.body:
Maybe you won your office pool. Maybe a bank erred in your favor. Maybe you got a refund on your tax return this year. What are you going to do with that money?

You could put it all in your savings account. Or, you could purchase a next-level, multi-thousand piece LEGO set, build it, and display it in your home. It's important to have priorities. And all kidding aside, it's also important to have fun, even as an adult.

LEGO was never cheap, per se. But particularly on the high end, it's never been more expensive. The company explains this by way of its quality pledge: that its bricks are tested rigorously against gravity, pressure, and anything else an adult or small child might subject them to – even human saliva. Combine this quality control with the 3rd party licensing agreements for LEGO's collaborative partnerships, and the costs quickly add up.

The cheapest LEGO set available is about $10. The most expensive LEGO set available is 100 times that amount. Here, for your morbid fascination and possible purchase, are the 10 most expensive LEGO sets currently for sale, as of October 2026. Hopefully, we won't have to establish an even higher ceiling in the months and years ahead. But we probably will.

TL;DR: The 10 Most Expensive LEGO Sets You Can Buy

LEGO The Lord of the Rings: Minas Tirith

LEGO Star Wars: Jabba's Sail Barge – Collectors' Edition

The slimiest, most decadent gangster in the Outer Rim has a ride to match his excess . You'll recognize Jabba's Sail Barge from Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi, where Leia, Luke, Chewbacca, Lando, and R2-D2 engineer a daring rescue of Han Solo, moments before they're to be fed to the Sarlacc Pit Monster. This set contains fully decorated interiors and 11 Star Wars characters, including Salacious Crumb, Max Rebo, Princess Leia in her slave costume, and of course, Jabba the Hutt himself.

See our list of the best Star Wars LEGO sets for more like this.

We built this set at the time of its launch, and we were impressed by its magnitude: six floors (not including the roof), of beautiful scenery and movie Easter Eggs, and 271 blue-tinted windows which form the building's signature facade. The LEGO Avengers Tower also comes with 31 Minifigures encompassing everyone that ought to be in a set of this scope in size – everyone from Iron Man to Hulk to Pepper Potts to Erik Selvig.

See our list of the best LEGO Marvel sets for more like this.

This is one of LEGO's most impressive and visually stunning – an example of what the company's designers are capable of when they abandon all pretense of a "playable" experience and focus almost exclusively on aesthetics and visual presentation. Rivendell comes with a complete Fellowship of the Ring, with Minifigures of every member from Merry to Gandalf to Legolas. Check out our feature in which we build LEGO Rivendell , as well as our interview with the LEGO Rivendell lead designer .

See our list of the best Lord of the Rings LEGO sets .

At 10,001 pieces, the Eiffel Tower is the biggest set that LEGO has ever released, with the Colosseum now coming in second with 9036 pieces. It is a repetitive build, of course – its use of arches, support beams, and cross-beams mirrors that of the actual building. But like The Colosseum, you're buying and building this for the end result – a beautiful model of a real-life attraction that's nearly five feet tall.

See our list of the best LEGO Architecture sets for more like this.

The newest Lord of the Rings set is the biggest one yet , showcasing the "White City," the capitol city of Gondor. You can build all the recognizable landmarks, including the Tower of Ecthelion, the Court of the Fountain, and the Citadel. The minifigures are Gandalf the White, Faramir, Denethor, Peregrin Took, Aragorn, Arwen, and four Gondor soldiers. It's more than just an external presentation too; turn it around, and you can explore the interiors, including a massive Hall of the Kings. We reviewed this set for its launch , and we think it's one of LEGO's best .

This display of Venusaur, Charizard, and Blastoise is one of the most fun-to-build sets in recent memory. It's three biomes with three respective Pokémon, and each creature is a full,. comprehensive build in its own right. You can display them seperately or as a single model by merging them together at the base. We built this set for its launch and highly recommend it.

We built the LEGO Titanic when it came out, and the designers treated it with the seriousness and reverence it deserved. The model has no minifigures – just the Titanic itself, with all its riggings, on a stand that's designed to look like classical wood. Separating the "unsinkable" ship into three segments gives you a good look at its cross-section; you can see the dining room, the crew quarters, and the boiler room. And you can also see the piston engines, which pump up and down when you turn the boat's propellers.

At four-and-a-half feet long, this model of Darth Vader's flagship is the longest LEGO set ever designed, edging out the LEGO Titanic by a half inch. It comes with a three pillared, hefty black stand, a minifigure-scaled model of the ship's bridge, and a tiny model of an Imperial Star Destroyer for scale. This thing is absolutely massive – there's instructions on how to transport it in its instruction booklet – and unfortunately, it has a price to match.

It comes with a cool selection of minifigures, including Darth Vader and six bounty hunters: Boba Fett, Dengar, Bossk, IG-88, 4-LOM, and Zuckuss.

It's difficult to imagine that a LEGO set would ever cost more than this Ultimate Collector Series edition of the Millennium Falcon. But then again, this set is something special, and its longevity speaks for itself. This particular model launched in 2017 – nearly six years ago, which makes it way past the age when LEGO retires its old sets to make space on the shelves for new ones.

It shows how far ahead of its time this set was at the time of its release. It shows how popular it continues to be; this is the definitive Star Wars ship. And it carries an impressive implication: that no LEGO designer has bothered to design a new one, on this scale, because the current model is so good. If you can only buy one massive set this year, this legendary "hunk of junk" is an excellent choice.

The most expensive set in LEGO history is this recreation of the Death Star, available exclusively at the LEGO Store. It is not a sphere. Rather, it is a massive crosssection composed of numerous dioramas, which depict the original trilogy's classic moments. It includes everything from the destruction of Alderaan, to the escape from the trash compactor, to the final throne room duel between Luke, Vader, and Palpatine.

The set comes with a massive superlaser on its side, and it stands nearly three feet tall. It also comes with 38 LEGO minifigures so you can act out any scenario. Make sure you have somewhere to display this behemoth before you purchase it. And if you're still hesistant, check out our full review of the build to learn more.

LEGO Star Wars The Mandalorian's N-1 Starfighter

LEGO Star Wars TIE Fighter & X-Wing Mash-up

Although many modern LEGO sets are still targeted toward kids, the adult market has exploded in the past five years. Many of the more expensive sets are marked as 18+ due to their difficulty and overall number of pieces.

The type of 'adult set' has changed as well. It used to be that the 18+ age recommendation was based on its challenge, and little else. Increasingly, it's come to signify

When Is the Best Time to Buy LEGO Sets at a discount?

LEGO sets can be really expensive, but sales can make the prices a lot more reasonable. The overall best time to buy LEGO sets is during event sale days like Black Friday and Amazon Prime Day . You can also usually find some great discounts on Star Wars day for Star Wars sets specifically.

Kevin Wong is a contributing freelancer for IGN, specializing in LEGO. He's also been published in Complex, Engadget, Gamespot, Kotaku, and more. Follow him on Twitter at @kevinjameswong .

articles.title: YouTuber's Channel Permanently Banned Over Censored Hellraiser: Revival Gameplay Video
articles.summary: A YouTuber and streamer's channel was permanently banned for a Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival gameplay video.
articles.body:
A YouTuber and streamer's channel was permanently banned for a Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival gameplay video.

French content creator J0nathan said that despite covering up the nudity in the game’s opening scenes with black boxes, his channel was removed for violating YouTube’s sex and nudity policy. “Explicit content that’s meant to be sexually gratifying isn’t allowed on YouTube,” the company told the streamer in response to an appeal upholding the ban.

Hellraiser: Revival, from Space Marine 2 developer Saber Interactive, opens with a raunchy sex scene featuring a topless woman and some BDSM play. Following that, the male character runs around for a while with their wang in the wind. While the scene is explicit, it’s essential to understanding the story and acts as the catalyst for everything that follows.

J0nathan claimed that this is the scene that got his channel banned, despite the fact uncensored gameplay of the same scene remains live on other YouTube channels. While he did add the "Not Made for Kids" label to the video, he did not age gate it, assuming that censoring the explicit scenes would be enough to satisfy YouTube.

"Since the rest of the game was just a standard horror title like Resident Evil I figured it didn't really require an age restriction, and that if anything, YouTube would just apply one later on like they always do," he said.

J0nathan had 190,000 subscribers on his channel at the time of the ban, which he told IGN was "permanent."

"My channel has been completely deleted, wiping out 10 years of hard work and destroying my main source of income," he continued. "I've never had any issues with the platform before. No warnings, no strikes, nothing. And yet they just threw me away like I was nothing.”

J0nathan said he has made attempts to run through YouTube’s appeal process, but “everything seems to be handled by AI.” His first appeal was rejected within a few minutes, and support accounts on social media responded with a generic message: "We've reviewed your case and are upholding our decision.”

“How can they possibly uphold such a decision when other videos showing the exact same scene without any censorship are still available on the platform?” he commented. “It really doesn't feel like any human being is actually reviewing these cases.”

J0nathan has a side channel but is afraid of using it because YouTube prohibits banned users from operating other channels. If he attempted it, he would run the risk of losing both channels. “I'm absolutely devastated,” he told IGN. “Beyond losing my income, I'm also losing 10 years of hard work and over 3,000 videos. The emotional impact is huge. Those videos represent a big part of my life, and losing them hurts more than I can describe.

“I've tried everything. I've reached out to my contacts, asked fellow content creators for help, but none of them have managed to get in touch with anyone at YouTube who could actually review my case. The same goes for the game developers. I've sent them emails and tagged them on X, hoping they might step in and help. I'm convinced they have contacts at YouTube to help prevent unfair bans related to their game, and yet they've completely ignored me.”

Ahead of Hellraiser's release, Saber tweeted to offer guidance to content creators concerned that their videos of the game would be at best demonetized, at worst get their channel deleted. Saber recommended content creators label all streams and videos with "appropriate age restrictions, sexual theme labels, and other necessary platform tools."

"You will need to adhere to each platform's community guidelines," Saber continued. There is no 'streamer mode,' Saber also pointed out on social media ahead of launch, "so context and intent behind your content will matter."

IGN has asked Saber Interactive for comment.

articles.title: First Look: Andy Weir Teases New Sci-Fi Audio Project Exoplanet
articles.summary: Get an exclusive first look at Exoplanet, a time-bending Audible Original sci-fi thriller produced by Andy Weir and starring Anthony Mackie.
articles.body:
Exoplanet, a new audio sci-fi thriller starring Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo, arrives next month and IGN can exclusively reveal the Audible Original’s cover art ahead of its November 5 release.

The project is executive produced by Project Hail Mary author Andy Weir and written by The Ninth Metal novelist Benjamin Percy. I spoke exclusively with Weir and Percy about Exoplanet’s massive production and how the story presents a unique spin on outer space thrillers, which is teased on the cover.

“Well, you see right there the first hint of three different timelines,” Percy says. “There's the staggered foreground, middle distance, and far distance [with] astronauts spiraling into this vortex. I hope that it sucks the reader in right away and gives them a hint of what's to come. I'm not going to say exactly what causes the splintering of time. That's a mystery that awaits you, but I think that there's this almost whirlpool current that's dragging you into that image. You see this image, you know exactly what you're in for.”

Exoplanet tells the story of what happens to a team of astronauts when their ship “is torn apart by a quantum anomaly, and each surviving crew member crash-lands in a different era on the same deadly exoplanet — hunted, alone, and running out of time. Chief Engineer Jeff Shaw (Anthony Mackie), aided by his virtual assistant (Ray Porter), must battle an unforgiving present, driven by one thing: getting home to his daughter. First Officer Becca Bang (Ariana DeBose) fights to survive a hostile alien past. Science Officer Logan Bowers (John Leguizamo) wakes in a machine-ruled future that shouldn't exist.”

“It is much more like making a movie or a show than it is like writing a book,” Weir says. “When you're writing a book, you're a dictator. You are in control of absolutely everything. But in a collaborative project like this, it's everyone. Ben gave a rough draft for Episode 1 of Exoplanet, and four producers hopped in. It's a very different form of creation than writing a book. And I would say it's very, very similar, if not identical, to making a movie because it's the same dynamic. You have a lot of people involved and frankly, a lot of money involved.”

Percy says that collaborating with Weir and the team at Audible was a chance to push his normal storytelling process into something new and exciting.

“Nobody wants to read Andy Weir karaoke,” Percy says. “I like to Trojan horse different genres together. So this is an Andy Weir space disaster that has the Trojan horse of time travel inside of it. That allowed me to honor Andy Weir's legacy because what I was thinking when I wrote this was like, ‘If I were Andy Weir, what is a crazy-ass sci-fi story I could tell?’”

Percy says Exoplanet’s jam-packed cast contributed more than just their voices.

“I refer to writing novels as an almost monastic experience,” Percy says. “And when you are working with actors, you have to understand that you're building together. So the script is a baseline, but when John Leguizamo comes in and starts reading and interpreting the text, you come to think about it flexibly and realize that through conversation with him over Zoom and through improvisation that you can make the storytelling even more powerful.”

Weir says he shares a similar collaborative process with actors, especially when it comes to the star of this year’s film adaptation of Project Hail Mary .

“Well,” Weir says. “I like to jokingly say that Ryan Gosling considered the script to be sort of a suggestion.”

Beyond movie star improvisations, Weir says his experience on blockbuster sets is in line with what he experienced while putting Exoplanet together.

“For Project Hail Mary, I was a full-on producer, making decisions, giving notes on the script,” Weir says. “I was there for the whole shoot. I was giving feedback on a take, asking the directors, ‘Hey, can you change this and that?’ And obviously, nobody had to do what I said, but people listened. So my experience on Exoplanet was very much the same as Project Hail Mary.”

Weir says Exoplanet is the first of multiple originals he’ll be producing for Audible and that his involvement goes far beyond simply giving a greenlight to concepts he likes.

“These stories are curated by me. If I like the idea, then I workshop it with [Audible and the writers]. I'm not just a passive observer. There's a lot of back and forth.”

As Exoplanet’s launch gets closer, Percy says he’s excited for listeners to experience the full scope of both the story and production.

“When you listen, there's a three-dimensionality to it,” Percy says. “You can hear something moving from one side of the room to another. Wear good headphones.” Exoplanet hits Audible November 5.

articles.title: Militsioner Preview: Flirting with a Colossal Policeman to Beat the Allegations
articles.summary: I've never played a game quite like Militsioner before. It's unnerving, moving around a town when you're always being watched by a giant who could squash you as easily as look at you.
articles.body:
The town and people have an air of mystery to them, which is intriguing.

You have a lot of freedom to go wherever you like and do whatever you like.

It's a pretty unique game, in my experiencce.

I've never done anything wrong in my life. It's really important you believe me. But here I am in the grip of a 50-foot policeman, and he's not buying what I'm selling. Not about what I didn’t do – because I'm sure I didn't do it, though I'm not sure what exactly I'm accused of – but about anything, including why I'm up so early. I offer some excuse about having a job. Do I have a job? I don’t know. You get nervous when a cop bigger than a house is holding you to eye level. It seemed like the right thing to say. The good news: I'm free to move about town. The bad news: I can't leave. I'm innocent and they’re not gonna believe me. I have to get out of here.

I've never played a game quite like Militsioner before. It's unnerving, moving around a town when you're always being watched by a giant who could squash you as easily as look at you. So when my friend – who is really a very large arm hanging out of a window; why is everyone else in this town bigger than me? – tells me they're a lawyer and the best thing for me to do is get out of town and wouldn't you know it, they've got a train ticket and they're willing to give it to me, well… Isn't that convenient?

Turns out it was a ploy to trap me in a house so they could eat me later, but if they wanted that to work they really shouldn't have left all these bricks lying around. One smashed door later, my pockets loaded down with bricks, a fake train ticket (I appreciate the amount of work my “friend” put into this, you know? They really got into it), and some stolen cash later, I'm out on the street trying to figure out how to get out of town.

What I like most about Militsioner is how much freedom I have to do whatever I want. I can talk to the Colossal Policeman (that's his government name, according to Militsioner Steam page) if I want. He's hungry and sad. Wants a donut, because of course he does. He's a cop. I give him an apple I found on the ground. It helps with the depression, but he still wants a donut.

Say I don't want to get him a donut, though. I mean, I do. I just don't know where to find one, so I mosey along and get into an argument with the person selling train tickets, who thinks I'm a murderer and won't be convinced otherwise. They're going to call the police – really, they could probably just yell; I mean, have they seen how big this guy is? – when I decide to skedaddle.

Not to be deterred, I decide to break into the train station, which goes really well right until our giant cop notices and threatens to get involved if I don't vamoose. Okay, I admit doing it in broad daylight was a little ambitious of me, but what else was I supposed to do? Try to track down the weird hand that I keep seeing pop out of sewer grates?

But that's the point. I can do whatever I want, deal with this however I want. I can try to convince the train counter person that I'm a good guy and friends with the cop. That doesn't work, but only because I don't know the answer to the question they ask to test me. I can wander into a pawn shop and sell just enough stuff to finally afford a vending machine donut, which I bring back to the cop. He's a little confused, but grateful, and our relationship changes. I imagine he only gets more confused once I try to flirt with him. Listen, I really need to get out of town. Maybe he won't arrest me if he likes me.

At one point, he mentions wanting to listen to music, so I find a guitar and bring it to him, intending to either offer it as a gift or try to play for him myself and cheer him up. Neither works, so we're just there, me holding a guitar neither of us can use on the shore, him sitting in the water just outside of town. No wonder he's depressed. I take the guitar back to the pawn shop and sell it.

Finally, with my demo time running low, I decide to use one of the benches around town to advance time and break into the train station again, this time at night. Maybe he won't catch me if he can't see me. I don't have a ticket or a plan for actually getting on the train. But I didn't plan to give a cop who was bigger than a house a donut, either.

When I awaken from my bench nap, the town is flooded. The water's up to my chest and it's rising quickly. I use a brick to break down a locked door, and search for higher ground. But the water keeps rising. Eventually, there's nowhere left to go.

After I die, I see a menu allowing me to spend points I'd unknowingly acquired by doing things to improve the policeman's mood. And then I realize I'm playing a roguelike. Clever.

The time for my demo is up, but all I can think of is what I'd do differently next time. Faster to the pawn shop and the donut, maybe. Hit the other parts of the map I hadn't seen. If I played it right, I might be able to convince the person at the train station that I knew the Colossal Policeman or figure out what was going on with the hand in the sewers. The town didn't seem big, but I realized I didn't know it well, either. It was a stranger to me. If I wanted to leave, I'd have to learn its secrets.

And what about me? Was I guilty? Why was there a gigantic policeman monitoring this town, anyway? Why had it flooded? If anything, I felt like I had more questions about Militsioner after playing it than I did going in. But maybe one more run would answer some of them. At the very least, I knew where to get a donut.

articles.title: AI Driving Game Demo Forces Developer to Take Out Bank Loan to Keep It Running
articles.summary: The developer behind Teach My Little Sister How to Drive, a driving instruction sim where you instruct a generative-AI-powered, dynamic NPC, has been spending $1,000 dollars a day to keep the demo working.
articles.body:
The developer behind Teach My Little Sister How to Drive, a driving instruction sim where you instruct a generative-AI-powered, dynamic NPC, has been spending $1,000 dollars a day to keep the demo working. “Over the past month, the number of demo players has grown more than twentyfold,” the developer said , via FRVR . “This growth has also increased our operating costs considerably.”

It all seems viable and a good business model so far. According to the blog post, developer Easy Fox had to take out a bank loan to support the game, which is powered by AI models. AI models costs can soar dramatically as the number of requests users make, which consume “tokens,” increase. Teach My Little Sister constantly queries AI as players interact with the game’s NPC to progress.

The developer plans to factor this in when deciding how much to charge for the game’s full release. “For the paid release, we plan to account for expected AI usage in the game’s price,” they said. “Players will not be charged separately for their individual AI token usage after purchasing the game. This isn’t because each player is particularly expensive to support. The total cost has increased because so many people are playing, and we have taken out a bank loan to help keep the demo running.

Teach My Little Sister How To Drive Screenshots

“We want to continue operating the demo and would love for more people to enjoy it. However, we are a small team of four, and financial pressure may mean we have to close the demo earlier than expected before the full release. We have not made that decision at this time.”

The game originally launched its demo in February, but interest from streamers such as thinknoodles has given it a popularity bump. The game is also popular in Asia, where there isn’t such a stigma around generative AI, which people in the West tend to hate because it’s a theft engine that sucks up the planet’s energy like Shinra.

Teach My Little Sister How to Drive relies on Google Gemini and ChatGPT to power its dynamic NPC, which follows your instructions, reacts, and disobeys, but the developers are looking into ways of allowing local AI models to step in for players “with sufficiently capable PCs.”

Companies making use of generative AI are starting to face reality. In a recent Axios report , one mystery company spent $500 million on AI tokens in a single month after failing to put usage limits on its account. Elsewhere, OpenClaw’s creator burned through $1.3 million in OpenAI API tokens in a single month.

There have been a few high profile instances of triple-A game developers either using generative AI or being caught up in the AI debate. Recently, Capcom had to clarify comments about its proprietary RE Engine being “AI powered .”

The publisher behind Arc Raiders came out in defense of AI use in Embark’s extraction shooter, but the team has since been making progress on replacing those stilted performances with human ones . Even games industry giant Activision has come under fire for AI usage in Call of Duty and its marketing materials.

articles.title: GTA 6 on Switch 2? 'That's a Conversation for Take-Two and Rockstar,' Nintendo Says
articles.summary: Will GTA 6 come out on Switch 2? The boss of Nintendo of America has responded.
articles.body:
Nintendo of America president Devon Pritchard recently spoke about the company's plans, from theme parks to first- and third-party games. And with the launch of Switch 2, the door is open to more third-party games that previously skipped Nintendo consoles (Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is one example). So what about GTA 6?

The Switch 2 is of course more powerful than its predecessor, capable of running games like Cyberpunk 2077 and the recent The Witcher 3 remaster. But could it run GTA 6? And, if so, will Rockstar Games release a Switch 2 port? After all, it's coming out on the less powerful Xbox Series S next month.

“That’s going to be a conversation for Take-Two and Rockstar, but nothing to announce on my end at this time,” Pritchard told Variety when asked about GTA 6 on Switch 2. Bah!

Rockstar games Red Dead Redemption, Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition, and L.A. Noire are already on Switch, but the developer hasn’t announced anything about Red Dead Redemption 2, never mind GTA 6. Would Manhunt be asking too much? Rockstar’s sequel, Manhunt 2 , famously featured platform-specific controls for pummeling in heads with the motion controllers, and that’d work nicely on Switch 2 and make any onlookers afraid of taking me on when I play it on the train.

“We have historically said that Nintendo is for ages 5 to 95, and that continues to be true,” Pritchard said. “We want to provide a diversity in terms of the types of experiences that you can have on the game system, and that’s really important for us.”

Nintendo’s upcoming The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches on November 5, just two weeks before the launch of GTA 6. It’s about as close to Rockstar’s launch any triple-A game has dared, but Nintendo knows it has a captive audience of dedicated fans who love its stuff.

A recent SNL skit parodied the double-bill gaming launches , calling it video games’ Barbenheimer. The one-two punch of Zelda and GTA 6 toward the end of the year really tops off a fantastic year in video games.

We’ve had good friend times with Big Walk , industry leading combat in Onimusha: Way of the Sword , the first essential Bond game since GoldenEye with 007: First Light , the tantalising tactics and deep social mechanics of Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Wave , and loads more. It feels like we’re at that time in the console cycle where the developers have learned how to get the most out of the machines, and now we’re seeing what everyone can really do.

Now Rockstar just needs to prove it’s the wizard it is and squeeze GTA 6 onto Switch 2 so we can play it on the loo. Please, Rockstar. I need this. On the loo.

articles.title: 'It's Every Motherf***er for Himself!' — The San Andreas Mission You Need to Play Before GTA 6
articles.summary: GTA San Andreas' Reuniting the Families mission has car chases, shootouts, and cops recreating Terminator 2. It's the level where Rockstar truly found its cinematic flair.
articles.body:
When Rockstar debuted its extended look at GTA 6 on Netflix, it was as if the developer had uploaded a one-off episode of a crime thriller to the platform. Sure, this was a gameplay reveal and there was certainly plenty of what was clearly a person playing a video game, but it nonetheless felt like a cinematic event. Compelling characters, building tension, slick action, and beautiful camera direction – it was as if Michael Mann had shadow-dropped a CGI short.

None of that will have come as a surprise. Rockstar has always had one eye on the movies – the game that shot it to stardom is a love-letter to Goodfellas, and its most recent open-world is the greatest Western never filmed. But the cinematic ambition we associate with the studio truly came to fruition in 2004 with Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas . Its predecessors, GTA 3 and Vice City, had been packed with references to classic crime cinema and voiced by genuine Hollywood talent. But that wasn’t enough for San Andreas. For this ‘90s-set Californian epic, Rockstar wanted to put you in the movies. And so it designed missions that felt like they’d been pulled from the silver screen.

There’s no better example of this than Reuniting the Families, the penultimate chapter of San Andreas’ opening act. It’s a highly-scripted, expertly directed slice of interactive storytelling that casts you in the leading role. And by trading the freedom of its open world for a tighter, more authored experience, San Andreas makes this gripping getaway feel more dramatic than any story the series had told thus far.

It remains true even today that the vast majority of Grand Theft Auto’s missions take place outdoors. This is a series built on the city sandbox. One of its most appealing facets is that you’re free to go anywhere – every road, alley, and freeway is fair game. Causing trouble in that mass sprawl of concrete and asphalt was simply what GTA was during the first two games of the series’ 3D era, which for the most part only permitted you to come indoors when an NPC invited you in for a cutscene.

But the indoors offers something the open-world can't: Control. Direction. Oversight. Rooms and corridors are the perfect container for scenes and set-pieces, untouched by the continual simulation of metropolitan life. And so it’s no surprise that San Andreas, with its substantially loftier storytelling goals, frequently sends you into buildings all over its digital golden state. As Carl “CJ” Johnson, you stealthily murder your way through a music mogul’s mansion, steal rifles from a sleeping weapons hoarder, and rescue a damsel in distress from a burning condo – all moments that, thanks to a stronger guiding hand and purposeful level design, feel akin to playing through a movie scene.

That feeling peaks in Reuniting the Families, a turning point for the failing Grove Street gang. With the rival Ballas having practically overrun the city of Los Santos with its drug pushing operation, CJ’s brother Sweet decides it’s time to pull together the gang’s fractured families. He’ll meet the heads of the sets at the Jefferson Motel. CJ and fellow gang members Ryder and Smoke will accompany him, but remain outside while the negotiations take place. Soon, a rejuvenated Grove Street will strike back at their enemies and reclaim the streets.

If only crime were that simple. As soon as Sweet enters the building, the police turn up in force. Ryder and Smoke scarper – “It’s every motherf*cker for himself!” – but CJ heads into the motel to rescue his brother.

Confined by the complex’s small rooms and enclosed hallways, San Andreas suddenly transforms from an open-world playground into a third-person shooter. The motel’s layout functions akin to a level in a linear video game, its corridors guiding you forward through a series of pre-determined moments and combat encounters. The tense atmosphere this scripting creates is apparent from the moment you load in – a fellow Grove Street member is shot to pieces and sent flailing over the hall’s upper balcony. Another lies dead in the stairwell. A woman runs for her life. As you head on up to the main floor, you’re hit by an unexpected jump scare: a SWAT officer rolls through the door and opens fire. You’re about to enter a criminal's worst nightmare, a house of horrors where the law is waiting to pop out from behind every door.

The motel’s corridors are lined with invisible trigger points, each one kickstarting a unique scenario that turns a generic video game shootout into a cinematic vision of a building under siege. A civilian runs from one room to another, crossing your line of fire. A door blows off its hinges. Gangsters light up troopers as they crash through a skylight. An officer hangs from an air vent to take you by surprise. As you inch forward through this maze of rent-by-the-hour rooms, it becomes clear that each square foot of it has been painstakingly crafted to ensure every second of the ordeal feels ripped from the movies. Unlike the movies, though, there’s no guarantee that the hero will survive. You still need to demonstrate some skill to stay alive.

Thankfully, CJ is no slouch; he can combat roll just as good as a pig in kevlar. This is the tool that will shift you in and out of cover, taking you from safety to a perfect firing position in just a couple of incredibly cool seconds. And there is a lot of cover – not just the 90-degree corridor corners, but laundry baskets, sofas, and upturned tables. This is a cover shooter map built two years before Gears of War made chest-high walls a trend. Naturally, such an arrangement demands an appropriate weapon. Armed with the MP5 that his enemies drop, CJ becomes John McClaine, the motel his own miniature Nakatomi Tower. Now I have a machine gun, ho ho ho.

After creating a small mountain of corpses, CJ finally reunites with Sweet and the pair make their escape. A rooftop showdown with a police helicopter would, in any other mission, act as the finale, but this isn’t any other mission. Sending the whirlybird to its doom is just the half way point. With every cop in the city on your tail, a lifeline is found in Smoke and Ryder, who suddenly pull up in getaway wheels. There’s no time to question where they’ve been or why they’ve returned to the scene of the bust. You hop in and call shotgun. Well, AK – you’ll need fully automatic fire for this one.

The mission’s second half sees the format shift from third-person shooter to on-rails turret sequence. And while the action has spilled out into the streets, the tight control allowed by an interior space remains: technically speaking, CJ is inside a car, its driver following Rockstar’s script to the letter. The journey is completely authored, and so it becomes a rollercoaster ride through Los Santos – the route specifically designed to take you through streets perfectly shaped for the oncoming storm.

Police cruisers give chase, their passengers pumping magazine after magazine into your car’s bodywork. Initially, you’re at the front of the pack, the boys in blue tailing behind, but that very quickly changes. Like a city-sized Disneyland dark ride, cops keep popping up on either side of the track – screeching out of alleyways or thundering through junctions. What begins as a simple “blast what’s behind you” becomes a 360-degree shooting gallery, demanding constant assessment of all angles for incoming threats.

The cops are on rails just the same as you are, which means you’re the sole dynamic component in this regimented excitement machine. And while you choose where the bullets go, almost every stunt has been planned – the train will always ram into one of the initial trio of interceptors, the first biker will always collide with its allied car. All pursuing vehicles have been primed to detonate, ensuring the whole ordeal is a chain of explosions triggered by just a few bullets. You’re the improvising actor on a perfectly choreographed action movie set.

If you’re going to make an interactive action movie for the PS2, then you nod to the greats while you’re doing it. A mid-chase cutscene introduces motorcycle-riding cops in a shot lifted directly from the 1997 Nick Cage classic, Con Air. As more bikers join the chase, they leap onto your car, just like the T-1000 did in Terminator 2. This kind of action is commonplace in a post-Uncharted world, but back in 2004, a cop hurling himself onto your motor and throwing a punch was one of the most exciting surprises San Andreas could throw at you.

A mission as grandly cinematic as this couldn’t simply end with the Grove Street boys getting away. A roadblock is easily surmounted by simply driving straight into the two officers, but as we’ve learned, the LSPD were trained at the Robert Patrick school of holding on tight. He’ll soon wish he’d let go. Smoke drives into a narrow alley, where a helicopter swoops in low, its spinning blades angled for the kill. The pedal hits the metal, and the officer is chewed up in what is surely one of the goriest moments in any GTA. The helicopter falls to earth, the boys in green bail out, and their getaway vehicle crashes through a nearby Sprunk billboard, dropping down onto the freeway where it smashes into a fuel truck. The giant explosion is, of course, mandatory.

Reuniting the Families frequently appears in conversations about the best San Andreas missions. It’s not difficult to see why. But it, and the design of San Andreas as a whole, is the starting point for one of Rockstar’s greatest challenges: how to balance the freeform simulation of a living, breathing open world with those cinematic ambitions. By the time of Red Dead Redemption 2, the gulf between these two styles became completely clear. While exploring its sandbox frontier, you’re given complete freedom to play your way. Your actions have consequences, of course, but that’s dictated by the simulation. When you’re on a mission, that freedom is almost completely taken away – in order to put you in the movie and tell the story it wants to, Rockstar needs you to follow the script to the letter. And as the possibilities offered by the developer’s open worlds have increased, the fact that those possibilities are stripped back during moments of storytelling creates a sharp contrast.

That’s not to say one side of Rockstar’s formula is better than the other. If nothing else, the fact that I’ve dedicated an entire article to how brilliant Reuniting the Families is should tell you that I’m a big fan of the studio’s approach to these cinematic story missions. They’re exciting. Thrilling. They have authorial intent. They put you in the goddamn movies! But, with any luck, GTA 6 will find a way to successfully marry the simulation and the story.

Even if it doesn’t, Reuniting the Families proves having two sides to a coin is a worthwhile pursuit, particularly if both halves of the whole are equally accomplished. San Andreas did amazing things with its city sandbox at the same time as creating linear missions that could be fantastic stealth infiltrations, home invasions, or explosive getaways across Los Santos. And it was those moments that really took us into CJ’s life. Those were the missions that made him feel like a real person with a story to tell. That time he saved Sweet from the cops? Man, it was absolute cinema.

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: Peacemaker Taking a Backseat as James Gunn Builds Out the DCU, John Cena Says
articles.summary: John Cena said Peacemaker is taking a back seat as James Gunn focuses on building out the DCU with characters like Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman.
articles.body:
John Cena said Peacemaker is taking a back seat as James Gunn focuses on building out the DCU with characters like Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman.

The wrestler-turned-actor behind the Suicide Squad anti-hero opened up about the character's future during an interview on Happy, Sad, Confused . He said he's far from hung up Chris Smith's iconic metal helmet, but as for when he'll return as fans await Peacemaker Season 3, he can't say much.

"No," Cena said when asked if he's been in costume since the last episodes of his HBO show premiered in October of last year. "When I put that helmet on, I told James, I'm like, 'Dude, I'll put this helmet on as long as you need me to. He makes me a better performer, so I love being around him."

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

Cena was one of the first actors to work with Gunn when he began his transition to a new DC universe in 2019 . Hot on the heels of his work with Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy, the filmmaker's work with DC was first limited to directing 2021's The Suicide Squad and, eventually, the Peacemaker TV show.

He's since become DC Studios co-CEO alongside Peter Safran and, as Paramount merges with Warner Bros., he's seemingly planted his roots at Skydance as DC Studios' co-chair . Like he's done so many times before, Gunn helped Peacemaker become a more recognizable face for fans, but Cena knows he's got more to worry about now.

After directing 2025's Superman , Gunn has returned to direct its sequel, Man of Tomorrow , which will premiere in 2027. In addition to his involvement in projects like Lanterns , Clayface , The Brave and the Bold , and more, the comic book movie overseer is also wrapped up looking to cast beloved icons like Batman and Wonder Woman. In other words, it's hard for watchers – and Cena – to pin down exactly when someone like Peacemaker might be able to return to the spotlight.

"Now, this dude gets to play with a whole box of toys, and because you get the whole box of toys, you have to address the really valuable ones first – and I understand that," Cena said. "So, here's a situation where I put my heart and soul into a character, an unknown character, and it becomes a fan favorite. I also know that it's OK. I gotta step back.

"Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman… There are so many valuable IPs. I'm not in a leadership spot, but if I was, I'd be making those plays first. That's OK."

Peacemaker received two seasons before leaving the status of Cena's Chris Smith on a major cliffhanger with Season 2 . While there's been no word from Gunn on a Peacemaker Season 3, as the character's actor denies having put on the helmet since, it's hard to say we've seen the last of the character just yet.

Like Marvel's cinematic universe, the DCU feels ripe for experimentation when it comes to cameos and spinoffs. The Peacemaker character has already shown up for a live-action cameo in David Corenswet's first Superman movie, and while his status is somewhat unknown, it feels like he could always show up for more. As far as his overall arc his concerned, Cena said, at least as far as he's concerned, there's still "unfinished business."

"There always feels like unfinished business," he added. "I retired from wrestling , but people are like, 'Man, but you can come back!' You know what I'm saying? That's all that is to me: It's a message that, 'Dude, you did good work, and I'd like to see you again.' Nobody's saying, 'Good f**king riddance, Peacemaker. Bleh.'"

Gunn suggested Peacemaker Season 3 wasn't a priority late last year , saying, "Never say never, but right now, no." Addressing the Season 2 finale cliffhanger, he added, "This is about the future of the DCU." All of that said, the reflective-helmet-wearing character remains "really important" to the DC Studios boss as the DCU continues to come together.

We'll continue to see the pieces of his comic book movie universe fall into place when Clayface premieres later this month. Lanterns just introduced its Hal Jordan and John Stewart with Kyle Chandler and Aaron Pierre, but fans are already speculating about who might play characters like Wonder Woman and Batman . While we wait to see what's next for Peacemaker, you can check out IGN's 6/10 Season 2 finale review .

articles.title: Battlefield 6’s Dead Space Event Has Players Storming Area 51
articles.summary: Battlefield 6 is getting a Dead Space event in time for Halloween. EA and Dice are calling it a “non-canon” event, which means the Battlefield 6 developer can go wild with it. Necromorphs in Area 51? Why not?
articles.body:
Battlefield 6 is getting a Dead Space event in time for Halloween. EA and Dice are calling it a “non-canon” event, which means the Battlefield 6 developer can go wild with it. Necromorphs in Area 51? Why not?

The Dead Space and Battlefield 6 crossover was teased earlier in the week, with the alien monument The Marker showing up at the end of the shooter’s Vegas trailer. Pax Armata will be pursuing secret tech hidden beneath Area 51 in the event, which will be decked out with assets taken from the Dead Space remake .

Players will be able to unlock unique cosmetics for participating, starting when the event goes live on October 20. You’ll have until November 7 to grab what you want.

The Year Ahead for Battlefield 6 | 2026 Roadmap - Screenshots

“Battlefield 6 is now one year old and what an incredible journey it’s been, from our Top Gun collaboration, which coincided with the return of Naval Warfare, to the launch of some of the most exhilarating maps in Battlefield history,” Battlefield Studios general manager Patrick Klaus said.

“And we’re just getting started, with Season 5 set to be the biggest yet. This has been an unforgettable year and we can’t thank players enough. We’re ending 2026 with a bang with three maps set in and around Las Vegas, a new way to experience REDSEC, as well as delivering on some of our community’s most requested features, with the introduction of Platoons and Server Browser. There’s never been a better time to play Battlefield.”

The new season sees players wage war across the Vegas strip, peppering the neon skyline with hot lead and baking under the desert sun. The area 51 map will also be playable across standard modes.

On November 10, another map will enter the rotation: European Casino. This close-quarters map will chew you up and spit you out like a real Vegas gambling den. Later, on December 8, Dice promises to “bring an unexpected chill” to Vegas, suggesting it’s about to get snowy in Sin City. Just go with it, it’s fine.

The REDSEC additions alluded to by Klaus come in the form of Rapid Royale, a fast-paced take on the battle royale across the Vegas Strip. Faster rounds, fewer players, and killing generates money you can spend on respawning back into the fight. This comes at the very start of the new season, which officially kicks off on October 13.

articles.title: Wardogs Dev Says PS6 and Xbox Project Helix Ports Should Be Relatively Straightforward
articles.summary: The team behind Wardogs expects to bring the game to next-gen consoles in the future.
articles.body:
The team behind Wardogs expects to bring the game to next-gen consoles in the future.

Although some would argue that this console generation has yet to meet its full potential, platform holders are already ramping up for the next one with Sony's PlayStation 6 and Xbox's Project Helix, though neither company has locked in an official release window. However, it does mean some developers have to start planning ahead, and one of those studios is Bulkhead, the team behind the new shooter Wardogs.

In an exclusive interview with IGN, we talked about plans for the game's eventual console release. Wardogs is currently slated to make the jump to consoles in 2028 , which begs the question: Will it release on next-gen hardware? Bulkhead says it's not even really a question.

"I think there's not too much to consider," said Bulkhead co-founder Howard Philpott. "We make the game performant, we're going to get it on the next-gen consoles. From our perspective, it's a straight port. So yeah, absolutely is the short answer, to be honest."

Senior producer Kane Allard noted that Bulkhead is already speaking with platform holders about the console versions of Wardogs, and doesn't anticipate any issues bringing the game to next-gen machines.

"We're obviously already in conversation with the proprietors of those platforms, and they're going to have certain criteria that we have to match, and I assume it's going to be the same for those other consoles as well. So from our perspective, if we get it on a base Xbox or base PlayStation, it shouldn't be much more work to get it on next-gen, and it should just be more performance. So I don't think it gives us anything new."

Last month, former PlayStation Worldwide Studios boss Shuhei Yoshida said Sony and Nintendo should make their current consoles last as long as possible amid soaring costs that have already prompted PS5 and Switch 2 price rises. Yoshida told The Verge that console companies needed to focus on sustaining their current hardware platforms for "as long as possible."

We know that a PS6 is on the way at some point . Previously, analysts had suggested a 2028 launch seemed likely, though Sony is yet to make any official indication of when PS6 may arrive — and as time goes on, that late 2028 release date feels less and less likely .

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has insisted Project Helix remains part of Microsoft's gaming plan, but has also said next-gen Xbox hardware will be a "family of devices." "We are moving to a family of devices for Gen-10," she said in a memo reported by Windows Central . "There is not one device that fits all. We will certainly have a great console first, but we also know that many players will be on the go. There are some things that we are the best in the world to manufacture, and there are other things that will we partner on. So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this."

For now, anyone looking to play Wardogs will have to check out the PC version, which is currently in early access. Next week sees the launch of Season 2 , which will introduce major gameplay features such as rain.

articles.title: Wardogs Dev Holding Back Certain Features Because of Xbox Series S, but Working to 'Very Low-End Hardware' Has Its Benefits
articles.summary: The developer of Wardogs has admitted that the limitations of the Xbox Series S have stopped it from adding certain things to the game, but insisted these limits have also provided some unique benefits.
articles.body:
The developer of Wardogs has admitted that the limitations of the Xbox Series S have stopped it from adding certain things to the game, but insisted these limits have also provided some unique benefits.

During a press conference for Wardogs Season 2, Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer said the team is "limited" by the Xbox Series S and revealed that this is one of the reasons why the game doesn't have dynamic weather right now. The new rain feature being added to Wardogs this month will be persistent throughout a match, meaning a storm won't suddenly roll through halfway through a game and lighten up within 15 minutes. It's a constant downpour.

"We are limited, as every dev is, by Xbox Series S," said Brammer. "As great a platform as Xbox is, it's a very low-end hardware for a game like Wardogs. We have to be mindful of these things we're putting in the game now. Performance is the reason we don't do it, but we would love to see it at some point. There's an ambition for it, but nobody is working on it right now."

Bulkhead isn't the first team to acknowledge difficulties around Microsoft's cheaper console, which launched alongside the Xbox Series X in November 2020. Moon Studio founder Thomas Mahler stated earlier this year that it was delaying No Rest for the Wicked's Xbox release due to troubles with the Xbox Series S . Baldur's Gate 3 also came to Xbox a few months late and required the help of Microsoft's engineers to get the game's split-screen co-op working on Series S .

Indeed, one of the questions facing Microsoft ever since the release of the Xbox Series S is whether it would be willing to allow developers and publishers to release a game on Xbox Series X only, leaving Xbox Series S behind. As it stands, Xbox mandates that video games launch on both or none at all, and that there should be main feature parity between each version.

Although Wardogs isn't coming to console until 2028 , Bulkhead is hyper-aware of how everything it puts in the game could impact consoles in the future. In a follow-up interview exclusive to IGN, studio co-founder Howard Philpott echoed sentiments about possibly adding dynamic weather in the future, but noted Bulkhea would have to handle it carefully to avoid tanking performance. He added that, while Series S has its pitfalls, it also lets the developer optimize the game for lower-end PCs.

"As for Series S, Joe is right, and it's not an industry secret or anything," he said. "It is holding back what developers can do in terms of pushing the boundaries because it's so far behind par in terms of the rest of the power of the rest of the consoles. So yeah, it's something we have to be cognizant of, but at the same time, Series S does actually give us that baseline performance.

"We were so heavy [during] pre-release in terms of talking about performance for PC, and what we didn't necessarily talk about [during the] press conference was how much Series S drove us to make the performance good on lower-spec PCs, because the goal is to get everyone to be able to play with all of their friends. There's an obvious financial benefit to that, so it's not completely altruistic, but at the same time, it is the goal. That is the point of the game: being able to play with as many people as possible."

Philpott also noted that Bulkhead has always imagined Wardogs as a multi-platform game. The team recognized there was heavy demand for controller support prior to Wardogs' early access launch, prompting them to quickly put something together. He stated that this support is in "an okay serviceable state, but really it needs to be a lot better." Senior producer Kane Allard noted that situation has prompted Bulkhead to be more "forward thinking."

"I think that's a good example of one of the things that bit us a bit and made us realize actually we do need to be forward thinking," said Allard. "We made the decision, as Howard said, originally we were releasing on PC for early access, and it was kind of an afterthough, we need to have controller support. And then we realized there was a massive outcry for it, and we had to look back at the systems we had and try and make them work with controller, and there was a fair amount of work there. And yeah, we did do it in the end and it was a little bit of a slog, but that did burn us a bit. And we then realized, yeah, we need to be really smart, build stuff with console in mind, with controller in mind, and we're taking that forward for everything that we put in the game."

It will be a while before Wardogs makes its way to consoles, but this is a major part of the game's journey. Philpott also said that Bulkhead hired a pro Halo player to help with controller support and ensuring that it gets an extra level of care.

Wardogs Season 2 will launch next week on October 15.

articles.title: Wardogs' New Rain System Will Have a Major Effect on Gameplay in Season 2
articles.summary: Wardogs developer Bulkhead has revealed how rain will change the gameplay in Season 2.
articles.body:
Wardogs developer Bulkhead has revealed how rain will change the gameplay in Season 2.

Next week, Wardogs will release its second season of content, which will also add rain to the game. This will not be dynamic weather, so don't expect it to be sunshine one minute and storming the next; matches that include rain will experience rainfall the entire time, from start to finish. However, this will result in some major changes to the game, with senior producer Kane Allard confirming to IGN that it "completely changes the game," and as a result, some players may not actually like this addition.

"It completely changes the game, and it's going to be positive for some players," said Allard. "It's going to be negative for others. Your play styles might be affected. That's okay. It's not like every map's going to be permanently rain. It's just going to be almost like a different game mode, so to speak. [It] could be that some people really love rain, some people really hate rain based on how you want to play. But it does bring a lot."

As for how things change, it's pretty drastic. The map is obviously darker, and your visibility is worsened. One developer even stated that he lost his sense of direction on the map because he wasn't used to the way it looked now. The storms will cause thunder, which can be strategically used to mask gunfire or other loud noises. Raindrops will make different sounds based on the surfaces they're hitting, including rooftops and helmets. Windows will also fog up, though it's unclear if that allows players to be less visible when hiding in buildings. The team has also accounted for destruction, meaning if a roof is destroyed, players inside will be exposed to the rain.

As for other weather effects, Bulkhead isn't ruling anything out, but it has to consider how something like snow would change the game both in terms of gameplay and how the game performs. Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer stated that there are obvious changes to something like nighttime, which would add flashlights, NVGs, and lasers. Maybe one day we'll get more, but it sounds like it may take some time to get added.

We've got plenty more on Wardogs, including Bulkhead on why blue team loses more, a new gambling mechanic for Season 2, and even word of a next-gen port. Wardogs Season 2 launches on October 15.

articles.title: Wardogs Dev Explains Why Blue Team Loses More, Confirms Plan to Address the Balance in Season 2
articles.summary: The team behind Wardogs has confirmed that Lonestar, AKA the blue team, loses more than other teams and is making big changes in Season 2 to fix that.
articles.body:
The team behind Wardogs has confirmed that Lonestar, AKA the blue team, loses more than other team, and is making big changes in Season 2 to fix that.

Since Wardogs launched in early September, there have been no shortage of memes mocking the game's blue team, Lonestar. For whatever reason, Lonestar tends to lose a lot, and there are a plethora of videos showing Lonestar players crashing helicopters at base and making fools of themselves.

Speaking exclusively with IGN, Bulkhead confirmed that Lonestar's win percentage is lower than other teams in Wardogs, but it has actually increased over time. Lonestar's win rate was roughly 10% during the game's alpha, but has risen to 20% in recent weeks. Bulkhead co-founder Howard Philpott noted that this is partially a result of players choosing to support Lonestar because they see it as an underdog challenge. He even joked that blue team's reputation was a bit of a PR issue.

"So originally, and this is key to not misquote, it was like 10% in the alpha," he said. "So that then led to the perception: blue is bad, don't join blue. And then everyone tries to click on green and click on red because they're competitive and they want to win. So they're going on the better team. More recently, it's closer to 15 to 20%. It's probably closer to 20% right now, where people have actively been joining blue team to try and make them win, which is quite entertaining to watch. But it's undeniable, they are losing more than the other two teams because of that perception."

Bulkhead is taking steps to remedy this with the launch of Season 2 next week . The biggest change is that they are adjusting spawns and rebuilding bases for all teams on the map Bakurani. Senior producer Kane Allard noted that blue team's reputation may have been compounded by the fact that they were losing significantly more on Bakurani, possibly due to map issues. As a result, they've chosen to shake up all of the spawns.

"We've moved all three spawns, so it's not just blue team have moved," said Allard. "It's blue, red, and green. They've all moved. The actual hot zone of Bakurani hasn't been changed. It's just the spawn zones. It's kind of revitalized the map, and we've seen from a data standpoint with our internal tests that it has evened it out. But yeah, as Howard said, there is a genuine PR issue with Lonestar, and there are a few extra things that we're going to be doing to hopefully help turn the tide of that, as well."

Some of those "few extra things" include changing the saturation on Lonestar's uniforms so they can blend in better, cash and XP bonuses for playing and winning as Lonestar, and even posters in the other teams' spawns encouraging other players to switch to blue team.

"Yeah, we are doing some fun stuff," said Philpott. "We're even putting posters like 'Lonestar needs you,' in the other teams' spawns. So yeah, it should be good fun."

In a press conference, Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer joked that, "if you're not playing blue team, you are in fact, a pu**y." So with that said, it is now up to the players to take these buffs and changes to try and change the perception of Lonestar.

Wardogs Season 2 launches on October 15.

articles.title: Dungeons & Dragons Is Going to Outer Space With Star Wars: Tyro Squadron, First Look at Official Art
articles.summary: Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft isn't even out yet, but Wizards of the Coast has already announced its next Universes Beyond release for the TTRPG – and it's Star Wars.
articles.body:
Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft isn't even out yet, but Wizards of the Coast has already announced its next Universes Beyond release for the TTRPG – and it's Star Wars.

WotC announced that something Star Wars was coming to D&D back at Gen Con in July, but at NYCC 2026, it confirmed a new adventure, Star Wars: Tyro Squadron, along with a new Core Rules expansion for the Galaxy Far, Far Away.

The new Core Rules will likely be as large in scope as the recent World of Warcraft expansion, with a ton of story hooks and new ways to play classic D&D classes, but we don't know anything specific. WotC did reveal some information about the Tyro Squadron adventure module, however, but even then, there's not much there.

Dungeons & Dragons: Star Wars – NYCC Art

According to Wizards of the Coast, Tyro Squadron will let players "take the fight to the Empire as part of a secret Rebel crew. Set during the Original Trilogy, these new stories unfold as Luke and Leia fight their own battles across the galaxy. Fly daring missions, explore new corners of the galaxy, and help shape the Rebellion’s story."

Just like with Star Wars: Zero Company earlier this year, this new D&D campaign sounds like it focuses on the seedy underbelly of the Star Wars universe, rather than the bombastic heroics of Luke & Co.

Star Wars seems like a strange partnership for Dungeons & Dragons, and it's going to be interesting to see how the team works things like blasters and lightsabers into the traditional high-fantasy TTRPG. But, with how well the team handled the World of Warcraft expansion, this new partnership has at least piqued my interest.

Unfortunately, it seems like we'll have to wait a bit to know exactly what Wizards has in store for its Star Wars partnership. It said it will share more information about the expansion at Star Wars Celebration in April 2027.

As briefly mentioned above, quite a few games in this list have earned high praise from us in the past. Each has a very different experience to offer as well, so you can have a nice variety at your fingertips.

Or, if you prefer platformers, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown can keep you company with a "fast and fun combat system, tight and satisfying controls, and stylish look and feel", per our review .

Psychonauts 2 is another game from this list that we adored, with IGN's Tom Marks calling it an "excellent successor to one of gaming’s most memorable action-platformers" in his review . On a personal level, I'm a huge fan of this delightful Double Fine sequel as well, and am always happy to recommend adding it to a gaming library.

These games are just the start of what's available with a Humble Choice membership, though. Alongside the eight total games you'll get for your PC library this month, you'll also get a month free of IGN Plus , which allows you to disable ads across the site, enjoy discounts at the IGN store, score free games, and much more.

Each month 5% of your Humble Choice membership will go towards a charity as well, which is a wonderful bonus to have with everything else above. This month, your money will be going towards HFC ( Hilarity for Charity ), which helps out families impacted by Alzheimer’s disease.
